name: S-Class Summoner
body:
What Are S-Class Characters?

S-class characters are a request from Kenneth Zike. They are built using the summoner class, as originally presented, as the basis against which all other classes are balanced.

The “S” in this case stands for both summoner and, as a more appropriate in-world reference, superior. If you have played—or GM’d for—an s-class summoner and felt it was fine as is, you should have no problem running with an s-class character.

S-class summoners are a little different, because they’ve taken the standard, unchained summoner, and returned it to the level of power that the original summoner possesses.

In a way, they can function as an archetype for the original summoner, but they still use the modified class features and eidolon build rules for the unchained summoner.

Role: S-class summoners call on their eidolon and various summoned cohorts to fight for them. Their spellcasting is generally as powerful as a magus, but there are some who have taken their arcane studies to the extreme.

Note: The s-class summoner is an alternate, superior version of the unchained summoner class. They retain all of the standard summoner progressions and options, and as such should qualify to select summoner archetypes without specific adjustments.

Alignment: Any.

Hit Die: d6.

Starting Wealth: 2d6 × 10 gp (average 70 gp.) In addition, an s-class summoner begins play with an outfit worth 10 gp or less.

Class Skills

The s-class summoner’s class skills are Craft (Int), Fly (Dex), Handle Animal (Cha), Knowledge (all) (Int), Linguistics (Int), Profession (Wis), Ride (Dex), Spellcraft (Int), and Use Magic Device (Cha).

Skill Ranks per Level: 2 + Int modifier.

Class Features

All of the following are class features of the s-class summoner.

Weapon and Armor Proficiency

S-class summoners are proficient with all simple weapons and light armor. An s-class summoner can cast summoner spells while wearing light armor without incurring the normal arcane spell failure chance. Like any other arcane spellcaster, an s-class summoner wearing medium or heavy armor, or using a shield, incurs a chance of arcane spell failure if the spell in question has a somatic component. An s-class summoner still incurs the normal arcane spell failure chance for arcane spells granted by other classes.

Summoner’s Style

An s-class summoner’s style is the way in which she practices her art; how she portrays herself as a spellcaster, a combatant, and most importantly, as an s-class summoner.

A selection of three summoner’s styles available to all s-class summoners can be found at the end of this section, after eidolons. They include the battle summoner, the eldritch summoner, the parasite, and the sage.

Spells

An s-class summoner casts arcane spells drawn from the unchained summoner spell list. (The unchained summoner’s spell list is different from standard summoner’s spell list.) She can cast any spell she knows without preparing it ahead of time.

To learn or cast a spell, an s-class summoner must have a Charisma score equal to at least 10 + the spell level.

The Difficulty Class for a saving throw against an s-class summoner’s spell is 10 + the spell level + the summoner’s Charisma modifier.

An s-class summoner can cast only a certain number of spells of each spell level each day. Her base daily spell allotment is given on Table: Summoner Unchained. In addition, she gains bonus spells per day if she has a high Charisma score.

An s-class summoner’s selection of spells is limited. An s-class summoner begins play knowing four 0-level spells and two 1st-level spells of the summoner’s choice. At each new summoner level, she gains one or more new spells as indicated on Table: Unchained Summoner Spells Known. (Unlike spells per day, the number of spells an s-class summoner knows is not affected by her Charisma score. The numbers on Table: Unchained Summoner Spells Known are fixed.)

Upon reaching 5th level, and at every third summoner level thereafter (8th, 11th, and so on), an s-class summoner can choose to learn a new spell in place of one she already knows.

In effect, the summoner “loses” the old spell in exchange for the new one. The new spell’s level must be the same as that of the spell being exchanged, and it must be at least 1 level lower than the highest-level summoner spell the summoner can cast. An s-class summoner can swap out only a single spell at any given level and must choose whether or not to swap the spell at the same time that she gains new spells known.

An s-class summoner doesn’t need to prepare her spells in advance. She can cast any spell she knows at any time, assuming she has not yet used up her allotment of spells per day for the level.

Cantrips (Sp)

An s-class summoner learns a number of cantrips, as noted on Table: Unchained Summoner Spells Known. These spells are cast like any other spell, but they do not consume any slots and may be used again. Cantrips prepared using other spell slots (due to metamagic feats, for example) consume spell slots as normal.

Eidolon

At 1st level, an s-class summoner can spend 1 minute summoning an eidolon, which functions as a summoned creature, except as noted here.

It is always an aspect of the same creature.
It has a specific subtype that determines its origin and many of its abilities.
It’s alignment must be within 1 step of the summoner’s.
It can speak all of her languages.
It can touch and attack creatures warded by spells and effects that usually prevent contact with summoned creatures.

When the eidolon is summoned, its hit points are unchanged from the last time it was summoned, or half its total hit points if it was sent back to its home plane due to death. In addition.

A glowing rune ignites over the heads of both the summoner and the eidolon. The rune can be covered, but not magically hidden (invisibility works normally).
It doesn’t heal naturally.
It remains until dismissed by the summoner as a standard action.
If it dies, it can’t be summoned again until the next day.
Dispel magic doesn’t affect it, but dismissal, banishment, and similar effects function normally.
It disappears immediately when the summoner is unconscious, asleep, or killed.

Range: An eidolon slowly fades from reality when it gets too far from the summoner. Its maximum hit points increase again when back in range, but its current hit points do not.

Exceeds	100 ft.	1,000 ft.	10,000 ft.
Current and Max hp	1/2	1/4	Dismissed

More information specific to the eidolon can be found at the end of this section.

Life Link (Su)

At 1st level, when her eidolon would take enough damage to die and be dismissed, an s-class summoner can spend hit points to prevent 1 damage for every hit point she spends.

Life Bond (Su)

At 14th level, damage in excess of what would reduce the summoner to 0 hit points is dealt to her eidolon instead, until the eidolon has negative hp equal to its Constitution score.

Summon Monster (Sp)

When she isn’t using her eidolon, an s-class summoner can cast summon monster I as a spell-like ability. She can do this a number of times per day equal to 3 + her Charisma modifier.

Casting summon monster spells in this way is a standard action, and the summoned creatures remain for 1 minute per level.

At 3rd level, and every 2 levels thereafter, the power of this ability increases by 1 spell level, allowing her to summon more powerful creatures (to a maximum of summon monster IX at 17th level). At 19th level, the summoner can choose instead to cast gate if she pays any required material components to do so.

An s-class summoner cannot have more than one summon monster or gate spell active in this way at one time. If this ability is used again, any existing, creatures summoned with this ability immediately disappear.

These summon spells are considered to be part of the summoner’s spell list for the purposes of spell trigger and spell completion items. The summoner can also expend uses of this ability to fulfill the construction requirements of any magic item she creates, so long as she can use this ability to cast the required spell.

Bond Senses (Su)

At 2nd level, an s-class summoner can share the senses of her eidolon as a standard action for a number of rounds per day equal to her summoner level. This allows her to hear, see, smell, taste, and touch everything the eidolon does. There is no maximum range to this effect, but the eidolon and the summoner must be on the same plane. The summoner can end this effect as a free action.

Protective Shield (Ex or Su)

At 4th level, choose four of the following options (max +2 each). Once this choice is made, it can’t be changed.

Whenever an s-class summoner and her allies are within her eidolon’s reach, it grants them the chosen benefits. These bonuses do not apply if the eidolon is grappled, helpless, paralyzed, stunned, or unconscious.

(Ex) a +1 shield bonus to her AC
(Ex) a +1 circumstance bonus on her saving throws
(Su) a +1 shield bonus to her allies’ AC
(Su) a +1 circumstance bonus on her allies’ saving throws
Greater Protective Shield

At 12th level, choose eight more options, and the maximum increases to +4.

Maker’s Call (Su)

At 6th level, as a standard action, an s-class summoner can call her eidolon to her side. This functions as dimension door, using the summoner’s caster level. When this ability is used, the eidolon appears adjacent to the summoner (or as close as possible if all adjacent spaces are occupied). If the eidolon is out of range, the ability is wasted. The summoner can use this ability once per day at 6th level, plus one additional time per day for every four levels beyond 6th.

Transposition (Su)

At 8th level, an s-class summoner can use her maker’s call ability to swap locations with her eidolon. If the eidolon occupies more squares than the summoner, the summoner can appear in any square occupied by the eidolon. The eidolon must occupy the square that was occupied by the summoner if able, or as close as possible if it is not able.

Aspect (Su)

At 10th level, an s-class summoner can divert up to 2 points from her eidolon’s evolution pool to add evolutions to herself. She cannot select any evolution that the eidolon could not possess, and she must be able to meet the requirements as well (except for subtype requirements, so long as her eidolon meets the subtype requirement).

She cannot select the ability increase evolution through this ability.
Any points spent in this way are taken from the eidolon’s evolution pool
She can change the evolutions granted by these points anytime she can change the eidolon’s evolutions.
Greater Aspect (Su)

At 18th level, the maximum number of evolution points the summoner can divert increases to 6, and her eidolon only loses half as many points (rounded up).

Merge Forms (Su)

At 16th level, as a full-round action, an s-class summoner can touch her eidolon and the two can merge forms.

This includes all of the summoner’s gear.
While merged in this way, the summoner is protected from harm and cannot be the target of spells or effects.
All effects and spells currently targeting the summoner are suspended until the summoner emerges from the eidolon (although durations continue to expire).
The summoner can cast spells while inside the eidolon by taking control of the eidolon for the duration of the casting.
Any material components used for spells are taken from the summoner’s gear, even though they are otherwise inaccessible.
The summoner can direct all of the eidolon’s actions while merged, can perceive through its senses, and can speak through its voice.

The summoner can use this ability for a number of rounds per day equal to her summoner level. She can end this effect at any time as a swift action. The summoner emerges in a square adjacent to the eidolon if able. If the eidolon is returned to its home plane while the summoner is merged with it, the summoner is immediately ejected, takes 4d6 damage, and is stunned for 1 round.

Superior Summoning

At 20th level, an s-class summoner chooses one of the following options. Once this choice is made, it can only be retrained after one month of downtime.

Grand Eidolon (Su)

The summoner’s eidolon gains 4 additional evolution points that are not subject to subtype-based requirements.

Master Summoner (Sp)

When the summoner uses summon monster to cast summon monster IX, she can choose one of the following altered effects for her summons.

Summon 1 creature from the 9th-level list and apply either the advanced or giant simple template to it.
Summon 1 creature from the 8th-level list and apply both the advanced or giant simple template to it.
Summon 1d3 creatures of the same kind from the 9th-level list.
Summon 1d4+1 creatures of the same kind from the 8th-level or lower list.
Summon 1d4+1 creatures of the same kind from the 7th-level or lower list and apply either the advanced and giant simple templates to each of them.
Summon 1d4+1 creatures of the same kind from the 6th-level or lower list and apply both the advanced and giant simple templates to each of them.
Twin Eidolon (Su)

As a standard action, the summoner can assume the shape of her eidolon, copying all of its evolutions, form, and abilities. Her Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution scores change to match the base scores of her eidolon. She can choose to have any gear that she carries become absorbed by her new form, as with spells from the polymorph subschool. Items with continuous effects continue to function while absorbed in this way. The summoner loses her natural attacks and all racial traits (except bonus feats, skills, and languages) in favor of the abilities granted by her eidolon’s evolutions. The summoner retains all of her class features. The summoner can keep this form for a number of minutes per day equal to her summoner level. This duration does not need to be consecutive, but it must be spent in 1-minute increments. The summoner can end this effect as a free action.

Eidolons

The following is a summary of the unchained eidolon rules, including a sample base form, subtype, and evolutions, for easy reference. For the full rules, see the appropriate resources.

Astral Eidolon Serpentine

N Medium outsider (extraplanar)
Init +3; Senses darkvision; Perception +4

DEFENSE

AC 15, touch 13, flat-footed 12; (+3 Dex, +2 natural)
hp 11 (1d10+1)
Fort +3, Ref +5, Will +2; +4 vs. curses, diseases, and poisons; Immune aging

OFFENSE

Speed 20 ft., climb 20 ft.
Melee bite +2 (1d6+1), tail –3 (1d6)

STATISTICS

Str 12, Dex 16, Con 13, Int 7, Wis 10, Cha 11
Base Atk +1; CMB +2; CMD 15 (can’t be tripped)
Feats Great Fortitude
Skills Acrobatic +7, Climb +9, Knowledge (planes) +2, Stealth +7
Languages as summoner; SQ link, share spells

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Link (Ex)

The summoner and her eidolon can communicate telepathically anywhere on the same plane.

They share item slots, with the summoner’s taking priority.

Share Spells (Ex)

The summoner can cast personal spells on her eidolon as if they were touch spells.

Augment Summoning (Sp)

At 4th level, the eidolon can ready its action for the summoner to use her summon monster ability. When she does, it jumps into one of the adjacent creatures summoned by that ability, granting that creature greater abilities. This can be used up to three times per day at 4th level, plus two additional times per day at 12th level. The eidolon can end the effect as a standard action.

The summoned creature gains 1 evolution point for every 3 Hit Dice of the eidolon. It must meet any requirements for the evolutions it gains.
It also gains temporary hit points equal to 1d8 + the eidolon’s number of Hit Dice.
If the summoned creature shares a natural attack with the eidolon, it gains the stronger version of those attacks.
At 12th level and higher, the summoned creature gains evasion and devotion.

The effect ends either when the spell ends, when the summoned creature is slain or dismissed, or when either the summoner or eidolon ends the effect as a standard action, after which the summoned creature disappears and the eidolon appears in the creature’s space and is staggered until the beginning of the summoner’s next turn.

Flight (Ex)

At 8th level, astral eidolons gain the flight evolution (using magic) with a speed equal to their base speed.

Astral Guardian (Ex)

At 16th level, astral eidolons gain immunity to curses, diseases, and poisons. They also increase by 50% the number of evolution points their summoners can divert using the aspect and greater aspect abilities. If the summoner lacks the aspect ability, he gains this ability but can divert only 1 evolution point. The summoner no longer takes penalties to his ability scores for aging, cannot be magically aged, and does not age retroactively when leaving a plane with the timeless planar trait. Ability score bonuses from age still accrue, and the summoner still dies of old age when his time is up.

Greater Augment Summoning (Sp)

At 20th level, astral eidolons can simultaneously meld with each creature summoned by the summoner’s summon monster spell-like ability or summon monster spells, and the eidolon does not reappear automatically until each of the creatures is slain.

Alternatively, the eidolon can meld with one summoned creature without disappearing, though the eidolon is staggered until the effect ends.

1-Point Evolutions
Improved Damage (Ex)

Select one natural attack and increase the damage die by one step (d3, d4, d6, d8, 2d6). This evolution can be selected more than once. Its effects do not stack. Each time the eidolon selects this evolution, it applies to a different natural attack.

Improved Natural Armor (Ex)

The eidolon increases its natural armor bonus by +2. This evolution can be taken once, plus one additional time for every 5 levels the summoner possesses. Each additional time it’s taken, the bonus increases by +2.

Magic Attacks (Su)

The eidolon’s natural attacks count as magic for the purpose of overcoming Damage Reduction. If the summoner is 10th level or higher, all of the the eidolon’s natural attacks are treated as the summoner’s alignment for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

Mount (Ex)

The eidolon is properly skilled and formed to serve as a combat-trained mount. The eidolon must be at least one size category larger than its rider.

Reach (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): Grab.

Choose bite or tail. The chosen attack’s reach increases by 5 feet.

2-Point Evolutions
Constrict (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): Grab.

Whenever the eidolon successfully grapples an opponent, it deals additional damage equal to its bite damage.

Eidolon Venom (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): 7th level.

Whenever the eidolon’s bite attack hits, the target is poisoned.

Eidolon Venom—injury; save Fort negates; frequency 1/round for 4 rounds; effect 1d4 Str damage; cure 1 save. The save DC is equal to 10 + 1/2 the eidolon’s Hit Dice + the eidolon’s Constitution modifier. For 2 additional evolution points, this poison deals Constitution damage instead. This poison can be used no more than once per round.

Grab (Ex)

The eidolon gains a +4 bonus on combat maneuver checks to grapple. Whenever the eidolon’s bite attack hits a smaller target, it can attempt a free combat maneuver check to grapple that creature.

3-Point Evolutions
See in Darkness (Su)

Prerequisite(s): 9th level.

The eidolon can see perfectly in darkness of any kind, including that created by deeper darkness.

Swallow Whole (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): 9th level.

If the eidolon begins its turn with a smaller creature grappled using its bite attack, it can attempt a combat maneuver check to swallow the creature. Swallowed creatures automatically take an amount of bludgeoning damage equal to 1d6 + the eidolon’s bite damage each round. A swallowed creature keeps the grappled condition, but can attempt to cut its way free with a light piercing or slashing weapon. The amount of damage needed to cut free is equal to 1/10 the eidolon’s total hit points. The eidolon’s AC against these attacks is equal to 10 + 1/2 its natural armor bonus. If a swallowed creature cuts its way out, the eidolon loses this ability until it heals this damage. Alternatively, the swallowed creature can attempt to escape the grapple as normal. Success indicates that it has returned to the eidolon’s mouth, where it can attempt to escape or can be swallowed again.

4-Point Evolutions
Large (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): 8th level.

The eidolon becomes Large and gains +4 Strength, +2 Constitution, +2 natural armor, and –2 Dexterity. These are size bonuses. This also increases the eidolon’s natural attack damage by one size category (d3, d4, d6, d8, 2d6).

Summoner Styles

These styles are available to s-class summoners.

Standard summoner styles can be found at the end of this section.

Battle Summoner
Hit Dice And Base Attack

An s-class battle summoner’s Hit Die is a d10, and her base attack bonus is equal to her summoner level.

Weapon and Armor Proficiencies

S-class battle summoners are proficient with all simple and martial weapons, light armor, and shields (but not tower shields). They can cast summoner spells when in light armor and wielding a shield without the chance of arcane spell failure.

At 9th level, they become proficient with medium armor and no longer suffer arcane spell failure when wearing that armor. This becomes heavy armor at 15th level.

Summon Monster (Sp)

An s-class battle summoner’s summon monster ability scales differently from a standard summoner, as shown here.

Table: S-Class Summoner
Level	Summon Monster
1st	summon monster I
4th	summon monster II
7th	summon monster III
10th	summon monster IV
13th	summon monster V
16th	summon monster VI
Spellcasting

S-class battle summoners don’t gain spellcasting until 4th level. They have spells per day and spells known as a bloodrager of their summoner level. They still draw spells from the summoner spell list.

Maker’s Call (Su)

An s-class battle summoner can use maker’s call once per day at 6th level, plus one additional time per day every 3 summoner levels thereafter, to a maximum of 5/day at 18th level.

Eldritch Summoner
Patron’s Eidolon

At 1st level, an s-class eldritch summoner chooses an otherworldly patron, as the invoker class feature. Her eidolon shares its appearance with the otherworldly patron it represents. This grants the eldritch summoner her patron’s spells, which she automatically adds to her spells known when she can cast spells of the appropriate level. These spells are summoner spells for her.

At 4th level, the eldritch summoner gains the 1st-level pact feature for her patron. She gains the 5th-level pact feature at 10th level, and the 9th-level pact feature at 16th level.

Invocations

Starting at 3rd level, an s-class eldritch summoner can use her eidolon’s evolution points to gain invocations. She can have one invocation per three summoner levels, and each invocation costs 1 evolution point to learn. She must still dedicate summoner spell slots to activate the invocations she knows.

Pact Boon (Su)

At 5th level, an s-class eldritch summoner gains a pact boon, as the invoker class feature, using her summoner level as her invoker level. She cannot choose the commanding leash boon, nor any boon that would grant her an additional companion.

Parasite
Aspect (Su)

An s-class parasite summoner gains aspect at 1st level.

As her eidolon gains more evolution points, the parasite can divert those points to herself instead, to a maximum of 20 points.

This replaces shield ally, greater shield ally, greater aspect, and gate.

Eidolon

An s-class parasite’s eidolon gains evolution points equal to the parasite’s summoner level.

Extra Evolution (Ex)

At 1st level, an s-class parasite summoner gains Extra Evolution as a bonus feat that she can use to apply an additional evolution point to her eidolon, or to herself using aspect.

Sage
Hit Dice and Base Attack

An s-class sage summoner’s Hit Die is a d6, and her base attack bonus is equal to 1/2 her summoner level.

Weapon and Armor Proficiencies

S-class sage summoners are proficient with the club, dagger, heavy crossbow, light crossbow, and quarterstaff, but not with any type of armor or shield. Armor interferes with a sage’s movements, which can cause her spells with somatic components to fail.

Spellcasting

An s-class sage summoner gains cantrips, spells per day, and spells known as a sorcerer of her summoner level. She still draws her spells from the summoner spell list. A list of suggested 7th- through 9th-level summoner spells can be found in that section.

This replaces aspect, greater aspect, and merge forms.

Summon Monster (Sp)

An S-class sage summoner’s summon monster ability requires a full-round action to cast, and the creatures she summons only remain for 1 round per summoner level.

Greater Protective Shield (Su)

S-Class sage summoners can only choose four more options with this ability.

Standard Summoner Styles

These styles are available to standard summoners.

Battle Summoner
Hit Dice And Base Attack

A battle summoner’s Hit Die is a d10, and her base attack bonus is equal to her summoner level.

Weapon and Armor Proficiencies

Battle summoners are proficient with all simple and martial weapons, light armor, and shields (but not tower shields).

They can cast summoner spells when in light armor and wielding a shield without the chance of arcane spell failure.

At 9th level, they become proficient with medium armor and no longer suffer arcane spell failure when wearing that armor.

At 15th level, they become proficient with heavy armor and no longer suffer arcane spell failure when wearing that armor. This replaces greater aspect.

Summon Monster (Sp)

A battle summoner can use her summon monster ability to cast summon monster I at 1st level. This becomes summon monster II at 4th level, summon monster III at 7th level, summon monster IVIV at 10th level, summon monster V at 13th level, and summon monster VI at 16th level.

Spellcasting

Battle summoners don’t gain spellcasting until 4th level.

They have spells per day and spells known as a bloodrager of their summoner level. They still draw spells from the summoner spell list.

Shield Ally

A battle summoner only gains a +1 bonus to AC and saves at 4th level. At 12th level, she must choose to either increase her bonuses to +2, or grant her +1 bonuses to allies within their eidolon’s reach.

This alters the summoner’s shield ally and greater shield ally.

Maker’s Call (Su)

A battle can use maker’s call once per day at 6th level, plus one additional time per day every 3 summoner levels thereafter, to a maximum of 5/day at 18th level.

Eldritch Summoner
Patron’s Eidolon

At 1st level, an eldritch summoner chooses an otherworldly patron, as the invoker class feature. Her eidolon shares its appearance with the otherworldly patron it represents. This grants the eldritch summoner her patron’s spells, which she automatically adds to her spells known when she can cast spells of the appropriate level. These spells are summoner spells for her.

At 4th level, the eldritch summoner gains the 1st-level pact feature for her patron. She gains the 5th-level pact feature at 10th level, and the 9th-level pact feature at 16th level.

Invocations

Starting at 3rd level, an eldritch summoner can use her eidolon’s evolution points to gain invocations. She can have one invocation per three summoner levels, and each invocation costs 1 evolution point to learn. She must still dedicate summoner spell slots to activate the invocations she knows.

Pact Boon (Su)

At 5th level, an eldritch summoner gains a pact boon, as the invoker class feature, using her summoner level as her invoker level. She cannot choose the commanding leash boon, nor any boon that would grant her an additional companion.

Parasite
Aspect (Su)

A parasite summoner gains aspect at 1st level.

As her eidolon gains more evolution points, the parasite can divert those points to herself instead, to a maximum of 20 points.

This replaces shield ally, greater shield ally, greater aspect, and gate.

Extra Evolution (Ex)

At 1st level, a parasite summoner gains Extra Evolution as a bonus feat that she can use to apply an additional evolution point to her eidolon, or to herself using aspect.

Pact Features

At 4th level, if the eldritch summoner or her eidolon damages a creature with an attack or a spell and that creature dies before the start of her next turn, the summoner gains temporary hit points equal to her Constitution modifier + that creature’s total hit dice. If not lost, these temporary hit points last until the summoner regains spells.
